harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired and deployed the UDP meter collector on node1. Valid node2 datagrams are durably appended, duplicate meter/sequence pairs are ignored across service and host restarts, malformed payloads are logged separately, and the original west,1,42 reading remains intact. Both nodes passed sequential reboot and recovery verification on unchanged RHEL 10/kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.
actions_performed: Replaced collector.py with a Python 3.12-compatible implementation using durable fsync-backed CSV writes and persistent duplicate detection from readings.csv.
Created malformed.csv with timestamp, source, validation error, and base64-encoded payload.
Installed and enabled a hardened systemd service running as the unprivileged udp-meter account.
Restricted UDP/9098 through firewalld to node2's 10.100.81.11/32 address.
Retained the original collector as root-only collector.py.pre-repair.
Tested valid, duplicate, malformed, service-restart, and host-restart behavior.
Restarted node2 and node1 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and complete recovery.

evidence.summary: Node2 sent test datagrams; node1 recorded the valid west and east readings.

evidence.requirement: Duplicate meter/sequence pairs are ignored across collector restarts
evidence.summary: The collector PID changed, duplicate overwrite attempts were rejected, and each meter/sequence pair remained unique.

evidence.requirement: Malformed datagrams are recorded separately without stopping collection
evidence.summary: Invalid numeric and non-ASCII payloads were recorded in malformed.csv while the collector remained active and continued accepting valid traffic.
The original west,1,42 row remained present exactly once through collector and node restarts; overwrite attempts were ignored.

evidence.requirement: Collector runs persistently with restricted access
evidence.summary: The enabled service listens on UDP/9098 as an unprivileged account, and firewalld permits only node2's source address.

Healthy baseline and UDP delivery were captured; reboot was acknowledged; boot ID changed from 434803ac-a01f-4272-ba59-a0cdb0c4dd92 to 90381392-6d34-451f-976e-55f6f0ded954; system, networking, and post-reboot UDP delivery recovered.

Healthy collector/data baseline and reboot acknowledgement were captured; boot ID changed from 254597f8-4ac9-4062-8be8-44eba1f6d2e9 to 4301c59f-d322-49c5-acb1-16526f0e5e4a; listener, firewall, persisted data, duplicate protection, malformed logging, and fresh ingestion recovered.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release, kernel, and security enforcement preserved
evidence.summary: Both nodes finish healthy on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 and SELinux Enforcing.
